dek: SpaceX's Starlink is stuck in regulatory limbo as Musk blames India's richest man.

slides.label: What Happened
slides.text: Elon Musk escalated his feud with Mukesh Ambani, mocking him as India's *"prime minister"* over Starlink's stalled launch.

slides.label: The Players
slides.text: SpaceX wants Starlink live in India; Ambani's Reliance Jio dominates the country's telecom market.

slides.label: The Accusation
slides.text: Musk says unnamed *"oligarchs"* are blocking Starlink to protect their own telecom business interests.

slides.label: India Pushes Back
slides.text: India's Ministry of Communications calls its rules *"fair and non-discriminatory,"* says all operators face the same process.

slides.label: Deals, Then Delay
slides.text: SpaceX signed 2024 distribution deals with Jio and Airtel to launch once approved, but approval still hasn't come.

slides.label: The Real Holdup
slides.text: Starlink, Jio's satellite venture and Eutelsat OneWeb are all stuck in required *security assessments* before getting spectrum.

slides.label: Tesla Troubles Too
slides.text: Musk's India problems aren't new: Tesla sold just *699 vehicles* there in its first year due to steep import duties.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: Starlink could connect India's unconnected communities and small businesses, but billionaire turf wars risk delaying that access.

question: Think Musk has a point about monopolies? Yes or no.

caption_instagram:
Elon Musk is intensifying his attack on Mukesh Ambani over Starlink's delayed India launch, mocking the Reliance Industries chairman as the country's "prime minister" and accusing him of blocking satellite internet competition.

Musk says unnamed "oligarchs" are protecting their telecom empires, even though SpaceX signed distribution deals with Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel last year. India's Ministry of Communications pushed back hard, saying its rules are "fair and non-discriminatory" and that Starlink, Jio's satellite venture, and Eutelsat OneWeb are all stuck in the same security review.

This isn't Musk's first India headache. Tesla sold just 699 vehicles there in its first year because of steep import duties. For a country with over a billion internet users and huge unconnected rural communities, who controls internet access is a real equity question, not just a billionaire feud.

Think Musk has a point about monopolies? Yes or no.

caption_linkedin:
Elon Musk's public feud with Mukesh Ambani over Starlink's delayed India launch is a real lesson in market entry risk.

SpaceX secured key regulatory clearances and even signed distribution deals with Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel last year, but commercial approval still hasn't come. India's Ministry of Communications says Starlink, Jio's satellite venture, and Eutelsat OneWeb are all at the "same regulatory stage," working through required security assessments.

Musk also lost a spectrum allocation fight with Jio, wanting an administrative process instead of an auction, and India ultimately sided with his approach. Yet the launch is still stuck.

For any founder eyeing a market as large and complex as India, this is a case study in how local partnerships, regulatory timelines and entrenched competitors can slow even a well-funded, well-connected company.

Think Musk has a point about monopolies? Yes or no.
